frase_inicial: Samantha and Ethan: your plan scores 82 and you own the house outright — there is a clear path forward.

tarjetas.frente: Retirement runs short unless something changes
tarjetas.reverso: Today your guaranteed income covers only part of retirement, so savings must fill a big gap; if you do nothing, the plan shows savings stop well before your life expectancy.
tarjetas.detalle: Savings and investments run out at age 73; yearly retirement shortfall about $115,335 per year on average

tarjetas.frente: College payments start now and press your cash
tarjetas.reverso: Ethan's and Ava's college bills take the same cash you could use for retirement, so paying college from bank accounts will shrink your cushion fast unless you choose a priority.
tarjetas.detalle: College funding still needed beyond current 529 balances: $98,837.55; Ethan starts August 2026, Ava starts August 2028

tarjetas.frente: You have a good emergency reserve, but it barely breathes after near-term goals
tarjetas.reverso: Your cash covers more than the recommended months, yet after the vacation and Ethan's payment only a tiny cushion remains to absorb surprises or a continued yearly shortfall.
tarjetas.detalle: Accessible cash $80,000; months covered today 7.9; cash above reserve and near-term goals $750

tarjetas.frente: Homeowners insurance is flagged as missing
tarjetas.reverso: The plan ranks adding homeowners cover as the top move because the home and car still show uninsured; confirm existing policies so a single claim doesn't touch your savings.
tarjetas.detalle: Top move: Add homeowners insurance on Primary home; score would rise from 82 to 84

tarjetas.frente: Most investments sit in one big US stock position
tarjetas.reverso: A large single holding and heavy tech exposure make your invested pot concentrated; spreading the holdings reduces the risk that a market drop wipes out the cushion you need in retirement.
tarjetas.detalle: VTI is ~39% of investable; plan suggests moving about $58,300 from that line toward diversification

tarjetas.frente: None of your savings goes into retirement accounts yet
tarjetas.reverso: You already save a lot each year, but it flows into taxable places; shifting some into the tax-advantaged accounts you can use changes how long savings last and how much tax you pay.
tarjetas.detalle: Eligible deductible traditional IRA up to $7,500; HSA available up to $4,400 if qualified; current contributions $0

tarjetas.frente: You run a small yearly cash shortfall now
tarjetas.reverso: Even with no debt and high savings rate, your plan year shows outflows slightly above income, which chips away at the cushion if near-term goals repeat or surprise costs appear.

tarjetas.frente: The planned 2030 home purchase adds another call on cash
tarjetas.reverso: Buying in 2030 requires a down payment and a mortgage payment after that; decide now how the down payment fits with college and retirement so one goal doesn't steal from the others.
tarjetas.detalle: Planned purchase value 2030 ~$562,754; planned loan ~$450,203.52 with monthly payment ~$2,995.22

tarjetas.frente: Insurance protects the kids if your income stops
tarjetas.reverso: Your term life and disability cover sit where they should: they would support Ethan and Ava if you couldn't work, so keep those premiums built into your yearly cash plan.
tarjetas.detalle: Term life coverage $2,000,000; long-term disability pays $150,000 per year gross ($12,500 per month); umbrella $2,000,000

tarjetas.frente: A choice you must make now: fund retirement or accelerate college savings
tarjetas.reverso: Both goals draw on the same cash. One path shifts more annual saving into retirement accounts; the other directs cash to college. Each eases a different future risk — you pick which risk to reduce first.

movimientos.title: Close a coverage gap
movimientos.action: Add homeowners insurance on Primary home so coverage integrity clears that gap

movimientos.title: Reduce single-name concentration
movimientos.action: Bring VTI from 39% to 25% of investable for the next concentration band — about $58,300 of that line

movimientos.title: Reduce growth allocation toward glide
movimientos.action: Move the invested mix from 85% to 80% growth (glide 80%) for the next horizon-fit band — about $17,100 of the invested book

siguiente_paso.titulo: Add homeowners insurance on the primary home
siguiente_paso.razon: It is the plan's top-ranked move and closes a coverage gap that currently leaves the largest asset exposed; confirming or buying this policy prevents a claim from forcing sales of investments.
pasos: Check current paperwork or call your insurer to confirm whether the primary home is already covered.
If not covered, get one homeowners insurance quote for the home value and compare one other insurer.
Buy the policy that fits and file the declaration page in your records; add the annual premium into next month’s budget.
